title: Monitor every browser task
description: Every page and task of the browser, whoever started it: your own and other agents' pages, the person's own tabs, the DSphere Chat bot's tasks and workflow runs, in every browser session and tab group.
guidance: Use it to watch what runs, report what went wrong (attention) and help where an owner is held up: pass a verification challenge, dismiss what covers a page, bring a failed task's page back to a usable state, tell the person (dsagent.page.notify) what needs them. Follow changes with dsagent.events.open topics [monitor] instead of polling. Reads of any page are shared (dsagent.page.observe / find / markdown on any pageContextId); to act on a page another owner holds, start an assist first (dsagent.monitor.assist). Never pass a sign-in wall, enter credentials or answer another task's question for the person. Read-only. Pages that need attention come first. The person can turn the monitor off (Settings, Browser Task Monitor): then it is refused POLICY_DENIED MONITOR_OFF.

attentionOnly.description: Only pages and tasks with an attention signal.

limit.description: Most pages to list; defaults to 100.

outputSchema.description: Every browser page and task, with who owns it and what holds it up.

pageContextId.description: The page, as every dsagent.page.* capability names it.

url.description: Origin and path only: no query, fragment or credentials.

active.description: The tab shown in its window.

session.description: The browser session the page is in: default (the person's own), named (sessionGroup new/previous; reopen with previous and sessionName), account (a managed application account's own session; open pages in it with dsagent.page.open accountId) or other (a session agents cannot open pages in, such as a workflow run's isolated one).

sessionName.description: With named: the session's name, for sessionGroup previous.

accountId.description: With account: the opaque application account id, for dsagent.page.open accountId.

accountName.description: With account: the account's label in the person's account catalog.

tabGroup.description: The browser tab group the tab is in, when it is in one.

ref.description: Opaque, stable reference of the browser tab group.

title.description: The tab group title (an agent or Chat task group is named after its task; a run group after the run).

kind.description: Whose page: the person's own tab, an outside agent's page (one opened or adopted for it), or the DSphere Chat bot's task page.

live.description: Whether its agent or Chat task is still working (always true for the person).

agentName.description: With kind agent and not mine: the agent's name, as the person approved it.

held.description: Who else uses the page: a guided wizard or a workflow run.

leasedBy.description: With owner person: the agent working on the person's page right now (its page lease).

taskRef.description: The task the page serves (see tasks).

attention.description: What holds the work up, each with who must act. Empty when nothing does.

code.description: sign-in-wall: a sign-in, one-time-code, consent or block page that only the person can pass; verification-challenge: a CAPTCHA, slider, picture or bot check an agent may pass with page actions (dsagent.page.action under its challenge budget, while the person's Verification Challenges switch is on); waiting-for-answer: a task waits for the person's answer to its question; paused-for-repair: a run waits for the repair of a failed block (dsagent.execution.handoff.*, only its starting agent answers); paused-for-resources: a run waits for host memory or CPU; task-failed / task-interrupted / run-failed: the work ended without its result; stalled: a running task published no step for 3 minutes (reported only, it stays its owner's).

waitingOn.description: Who must act for it to clear: the person, an agent (the owner, or one assisting), or nobody (the work ended; report it).

since.description: Since when (ISO 8601), when the owner says.

detail.description: A typed, value-free detail: the wall type, the run endpoint, the failure code.

blocked.description: Whether the page's work is held up (a signal other than stalled, on the page or its task): what dsagent.monitor.assist requires.

assist.description: yours: you assist here now; held-by-another-agent: another agent does; available: dsagent.monitor.assist start lets you act here; not-needed: you may act with dsagent.page.* already (your page, your lease, your run's repair, the person's free page, an agent page whose owner is gone); owner-working: its owner works and nothing holds it up, so leave it.

assistExpiresAt.description: With an assist: when it lapses unless started again (ISO 8601).

pages.description: Open tabs, those needing attention first.

items.description: One task running (or just ended) in the browser.

taskRef.description: Opaque, stable reference of the task.

kind.description: An outside agent's task (its connection to DSphere), a DSphere Chat bot task, or a workflow run (started by the person, a schedule, the Chat bot or an agent).

mine.description: Your own task, or a run you started.

ownerName.description: The outside agent that owns the task or started the run, when one did.

description.description: The task as its owner described it (an agent's taskDescription, the Chat request), or the run's workflow name.

status.description: Its owner's status: a Chat or agent task phase (planning, acting, paused-auth, awaiting-user, failed…), a run status (running, paused-auth-interrupt, paused-agent-repair, failed…), or running / ended for an agent connection.

attention.description: What holds the work up, each with who must act. Empty when nothing does.

code.description: sign-in-wall: a sign-in, one-time-code, consent or block page that only the person can pass; verification-challenge: a CAPTCHA, slider, picture or bot check an agent may pass with page actions (dsagent.page.action under its challenge budget, while the person's Verification Challenges switch is on); waiting-for-answer: a task waits for the person's answer to its question; paused-for-repair: a run waits for the repair of a failed block (dsagent.execution.handoff.*, only its starting agent answers); paused-for-resources: a run waits for host memory or CPU; task-failed / task-interrupted / run-failed: the work ended without its result; stalled: a running task published no step for 3 minutes (reported only, it stays its owner's).

waitingOn.description: Who must act for it to clear: the person, an agent (the owner, or one assisting), or nobody (the work ended; report it).

since.description: Since when (ISO 8601), when the owner says.

detail.description: A typed, value-free detail: the wall type, the run endpoint, the failure code.

tasks.description: Tasks and runs in the browser.
